verified_clean: Nemesis DECODER is byte-identical to the game-accurate oracle (clownnemesis v1.1.1 at /home/volence/sonic_hacks/sonic_hack/tools/nemdec -d) on all 156 files in /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm/artnem — 0 disagreements. src/core/compress/nemesis.ts:21-101.

Nemesis ENCODER (the 9579a3b XOR + package-merge work) produces streams the game-accurate oracle decodes back to the exact input, for all 156 real artnem files and 301 synthetic/adversarial cases — 0 failures. This is the strongest available check: it validates against Sega's decoder semantics, not just Aurora's own decoder. nemesis.ts:306-364.

Nemesis emitted code-table invariants hold on every one of those 301 stress cases: every code length is 1..8, every code value fits its declared bit width, the set is prefix-free, the Kraft sum never exceeds the 252 units left after reserving the escape, and no code's left-aligned top 6 bits ever equal 0b111111 (the 0x3F inline escape). The ESCAPE_UNITS=4 reservation at nemesis.ts:192-242 genuinely prevents the collision the comment claims — including the worst case, all 128 (nibble,runlen) symbols at uniform frequency, where package-merge yields all-7-bit codes (Kraft 256) and fitCodespace correctly lengthens exactly 4 symbols to reach 252.

Nemesis edge cases all round-trip through BOTH Aurora and the native oracle: zero-length input (encodes to the 3-byte 00 00 FF and decodes to 0 bytes), single all-zero tile, single all-$F tile, single ramp tile, 256 all-zero tiles, 256 all-$FF tiles, alternating 0/F nibbles, 4096 mixed tiles. Non-multiple-of-32 input is rejected with a clear NemesisError (nemesis.ts:322).

Nemesis XOR mode's cross-tile chain is correct: xorDelta (nemesis.ts:278-291) initialises prev=0 and never resets at a 32-byte boundary, matching the decoder's prevRow at nemesis.ts:65-75, and the oracle confirms this on multi-tile inputs (a per-tile reset would have corrupted from tile 2 onward). The mode decision at nemesis.ts:309 (`xor.length < plain.length ? xor : plain`) can never pick a worse encoding.

Nemesis re-encode size across ALL 156 real artnem files: 180889 -> 185824 bytes total (1.0273x). No file exceeds 1.285x and none exceeds its own raw tile size. The 1.10x guard at s1-compression-goldens.test.ts:208-218 is a real guard for the seven `8x8 - *` zone files (they re-encode at 1.02-1.05x and a plain-mode regression measured 2.1-3.0x would fail it); the 22 smaller object-art files that land in 1.10-1.29x are outside that test's glob but are all below raw size.
Kosinski DECODER matches Clownacy's accurate-kosinski (kosinski-decompress) byte-for-byte on all 9 real .kos files (8 in s1disasm/map256, 1 in s1disasm/artkos). src/core/formats/kosinski.ts:12-83.

Kosinski ENCODER is verified bidirectionally against the accurate reference: Aurora's compressed output decodes correctly under accurate-kosinski's decompressor, AND accurate-kosinski's compressed output decodes correctly under Aurora's decompressor, for all 9 real files. Descriptor-field placement (kosinski.ts:106-111) survives the case where the 16-bit descriptor completes mid-operation, and the short/full/extended match encodings at kosinski.ts:139-152 match the decoder's distance reconstruction at kosinski.ts:58-73 exactly.
Kosinski encoder output is slightly SMALLER than Sega's on every real file (e.g. GHZ 8378 vs 8464, MZ REV00 6013 vs 6080), so unlike Enigma it poses no ROM-growth risk on save (s1-io.ts:510).

Kosinski-MODULED decoder matches kosinskim-decompress on all 95 real KosinskiM assets in /home/volence/sonic_hacks/skdisasm, and all 95 round-trip through Aurora's own compress+decompress byte-for-byte. The 0x1000 module split and the (pos-2)%0x10 alignment at kosinski.ts:170/189 are correct.

The action dispatch at enigma.ts:70, the terminator disambiguation at enigma.ts:73, and the getInlineValue bit layout at enigma.ts:55-64 are all correct. The decoder is also bounded on corrupt input (>=7 bits consumed per iteration, readByte throws at EOF at enigma.ts:28) — it cannot hang the way Kosinski can.

The emitCompressed self-check gate at src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:398-417 is a REAL gate, not a no-op: it re-decodes with the always-real decoder and routes to `errors` instead of `files` on any mismatch or throw. The 12 files it throws on (lz*pf*.bin, sbz1pf*.bin) are LZ/SBZ moving-PLATFORM position tables — a different 6-byte-record format with no 0xFFFF terminator — not object layouts, so the throw is correct behaviour rather than a defect.

Genesis palette codec is an exact inverse for all 8 three-bit levels (encodeGenesisColor(decodeGenesisColor(w)) === w; the 255/7 rounding at palette.ts:12-14 and 25 round-trips cleanly), and all 1388 colour words across every file in s1disasm/palette lie inside the 0x0EEE mask, so re-encoding cannot silently drop any bit real S1 data uses. findings.title: kosinskiDecompress loops without bound on malformed input — exhausts the heap and kills the process
findings.claim: kosinskiDecompress has no EOF error, no output cap and no iteration guard, so a .kos file whose descriptor words are zero decodes forever, growing an unbounded JS array until V8 aborts the process — which no try/catch can intercept.
findings.evidence: kosinski.ts:20-23 readByte() returns 0 once readPos passes the end instead of throwing (contrast nemesis.ts:26, which throws 'Unexpected end of Nemesis data'). kosinski.ts:47-80 is a `for(;;)` whose ONLY exit is the full-match terminator at line 66 (`count === 1` after `hi&7 === 0`). With an all-zero descriptor: popDescriptor() -> false (not literal), popDescriptor() -> false (short match), count=2, distance=(0^0xFF)+1=0x100, two bytes appended per iteration, terminator never reachable. Executed repro at the pinned commit: `kosinskiDecompress(new Uint8Array([0x00,0x00]))` under `node --max-old-space-size=800` printed 'FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory' and dumped core (exit 134) after ~3s. An all-zero file of ANY length behaves identically (every descriptor read is 0x0000). Reachable unguarded at src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:285 `kosinskiDecompress(await readBytes(paths.chunks))` — the S1 open path over the user's own disasm tree — and at src/core/formats/chunk-mappings.ts:116-117 (importChunks, both chunk and block files). Related silent-corruption sibling on the same path: kosinski.ts:77 indexes `window[(writePos - distance) % SIZE]`, which is negative before enough output exists, yielding `undefined & 0xFF` = 0 rather than an error. Note: I truncated the real GHZ.kos at 88 different offsets and none ran away, so the trigger is a zero/near-zero descriptor stream (empty-but-created file, zero-padded placeholder, wrong-file path), not arbitrary truncation.
findings.fix: Make kosinski.ts:20-23 throw a KosinskiError at EOF like nemesis.ts:26 does, and add an output ceiling to the decode loop (e.g. reject once output.length exceeds a caller-supplied max or a hard 4 MB) so a corrupt file surfaces as a routed error instead of an unrecoverable process abort. Also make the negative-window read at line 77 an explicit error rather than a silent zero.

verdict.reasoning:
Attempted refutation on four links; all held.

TRACE (kosinski.ts:47-80): with an all-zero descriptor, popDescriptor() -> false (not literal), popDescriptor() -> false (short-match branch, line 69), count=2, distance=(0^0xFF)+1=0x100, two bytes appended per iteration. The only break is line 66, which lives inside the FULL-match branch (requires line 54's popDescriptor() to be true) and is therefore unreachable. readByte() (line 21) returns 0 past EOF rather than throwing, so getDescriptor() at line 41 refills descriptor with 0x0000 forever. output: number[] grows without bound.

EXECUTED at pinned SHA 2b38e0b: esbuild-transpiled the unmodified src/core/formats/kosinski.ts and ran kosinskiDecompress under node --max-old-space-size. Inputs new Uint8Array(0), [0x00,0x00], and new Uint8Array(4096) each printed "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory" and dumped core. A control input (60 bytes of shell-script text) returned normally in 0ms, confirming the harness is sound and the failure is input-dependent.

GUARDS CHECKED AND INSUFFICIENT:
- src/core/project/s1/index.ts:368 `if (!meta.available)` — the most likely refutation. Availability comes from resolveEntry (lines 178-196), which is pure `fa.exists()`. Presence only; never size or content. A zero-byte/placeholder chunks file resolves as available:true.
- src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:221-229 readBytes throws only ENOENT for a missing prefetch entry; an existing empty file passes through to line 285 unguarded.
- src/renderer/providers/chunk-library-import.ts:28 try/catch is inert against a V8 heap abort, exactly as the seat claimed.

CORRECTION THAT WIDENS THE FINDING: the seat characterized the trigger as "a zero/near-zero descriptor stream". Too narrow. A git-lfs pointer file (ordinary non-zero ASCII, "version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1\noid sha256:...\nsize 1234\n") ran away identically. The true trigger class is any input whose descriptor bits never route to the full-match terminator before EOF, which includes plain text — making an LFS-pointer clone of a disasm tree a realistic path to the crash.

SIBLING CLAIM CONFIRMED: (0-256)%8192 === -256 in JS, window[-256] is undefined, and writeByte's `byte & 0xFF` converts NaN to 0. Silent zero, no error. Only reachable on malformed input (valid Kosinski never back-references before stream start), so it is a robustness wart rather than a corruption risk on real files.

Both cited call sites match the report verbatim: s1-io.ts:285 and chunk-mappings.ts:116-117.
verdict.severity_correction: No change — "high" is correct as stated. Recording the reasoning since I checked it both directions: it fails the "critical" bar because the failure is a loud process abort, not silent loss or corruption of data at rest; it clears the "high" bar because two main-path features (S1 project open, chunk import) kill the process instead of routing an error. Triage note: the chunk-import path is the one that costs real work, since it runs in the renderer mid-session and the abort takes unsaved editor state with it, whereas the open path fails before edits exist.

findings.title: kosinskiModuledCompress cannot express two size classes; the sprite-export path that uses it has no self-check
findings.claim: kosinskiModuledCompress writes the decompressed size as a bare 2-byte big-endian field, so an input of exactly 0xA000 bytes collides with the format's 0xA000->0x8000 sentinel (8192 bytes silently lost) and any input >= 0x10000 wraps to a header of 0x0000 (everything lost), and the only caller that can hit it does no round-trip verification.
findings.evidence: kosinski.ts:166 `const out = [input.length >> 8 & 0xff, input.length & 0xff]` — no range check. kosinski.ts:179 `const size = rawSize === 0xa000 ? 0x8000 : rawSize` is the sentinel the write side ignores. Measured at the pinned commit: 40960-byte input -> header 0xa000 -> Aurora's own kosinskiModuledDecompress returns 32768 bytes, AND the game-accurate oracle /home/volence/sonic_hacks/programs/accurate-kosinski/build/kosinskim-decompress returns 32768 bytes too, so this is real data loss and not just a self-consistency gap; 65536-byte input -> header 0x0000 -> both Aurora and the oracle return 0 bytes. 0x8000, 0x7FFF, 0xA001, 0x1000, 0x1001, empty and 1-byte all round-trip clean, so the failure is exactly the two classes above. Reachability: src/core/compress/index.ts:19 maps 'kosinski-moduled' to this pair; src/core/export/sprite-export.ts:94 `compressionFor(adapter.artCompression)` then lines 101/107 `codec.compress(serializeTiles(...))` with NO re-decode comparison — unlike src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:405-415 and src/core/formats/games/s1-art-write.ts:118-127, which both gate. src/renderer/components/sprite/SpriteMode.tsx:44 makes 'kosinski-moduled' the default for the s3k target. Largest real S3K KosinskiM asset measured is 0x7000 (SK Sonic Knuckles), so stock data never trips it — an Aurora-authored sheet is the exposure.
findings.fix: Throw from kosinskiModuledCompress when input.length >= 0x10000 or === 0xA000 (or emit the 0xA000 case as the sentinel the decoder expects), and wrap sprite-export.ts:101/107 in the same re-decode-and-compare gate that emitCompressed and encodeS1ArtWriteBack already use.

findings.title: Enigma encoder inflates every re-saved map16 file 1.33x-2.0x, and unlike Nemesis has no size-regression test
findings.claim: enigmaCompress emits every word as a full 16-bit inline raw-copy, never using the incremental/literal/run packets the format exists for, so saving blocks writes a substantially LARGER file back into the user's disasm — the exact ROM-growth hazard the Nemesis golden test was written to prevent, with no equivalent guard here.
findings.evidence: enigma.ts:127 hard-codes the header to TOTAL_INLINE_BITS=11 / RENDER_FLAGS_MASK=0x1f (all 16 bits inline) and enigma.ts:146-155 emits only action-5 packets, ~17 bits/word. Measured against real s1disasm files (decode matched the clownlzss oracle exactly on all 12, and the oracle decodes our output correctly, so this is size only, not correctness): map16/GHZ.eni 2464 -> 3624 (1.47x), map16/LZ.eni 810 -> 1622 (2.00x), map16/MZ.eni 2058 -> 3072, map16/SBZ.eni 3738 -> 4964, map16/SLZ.eni 2020 -> 3416, map16/SYZ.eni 2414 -> 3556; tilemaps run 3.45x-12.18x. src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:497 writes this on every `dirty.blocks` save. The ROM hazard the Nemesis test cites is real — I verified /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm/s1.sounddriver.asm:2853-2856 does contain `; Don't let Sega sample cross $8000-byte boundary` / `align $8000` — but the corresponding size assertion exists only for Nemesis (s1-compression-goldens.test.ts:208-218, `< 1.10`, and only over the seven `8x8 - *.nem` files); there is no Enigma size test at all in src/core/formats/classic/__tests__/enigma.test.ts. Editing one block therefore grows GHZ's map16 by 1160 bytes.
findings.fix: Add run detection to enigmaCompress — at minimum action 2 (inline-same) for repeated words and action 3 (inline-increment) for ascending runs, plus a per-file inline-bit width computed from the actual maximum tile index instead of a fixed 11 — and pin the result with a golden test asserting re-encoded size <= original for every s1disasm map16/*.eni, mirroring the Nemesis test.

findings.title: nemesisCompress silently wraps the 15-bit tile count above 0x8000 tiles
findings.claim: encodeNemesis masks the tile count into the header's 15-bit field with no range check, so a >= 1 MiB tile pool produces a header claiming 0 tiles and a stream that decodes to nothing.
findings.evidence: nemesis.ts:333 `out.push(((tileCount >> 8) & 0x7f) | (xorMode ? 0x80 : 0), tileCount & 0xff)` — the `& 0x7f` discards bit 15 upward, and nemesis.ts:322-323 only validates length % 32. Measured: a 0x8000-tile (1048576-byte) input encodes to a header whose nemesisHeader().tileCount is 0 and nemesisDecompress returns 0 bytes. Both present call sites do catch it as a save failure rather than corruption — s1-io.ts:405-415 emitCompressed re-decodes and pushes an error, s1-art-write.ts:120-123 compares back.length and returns ok:false — so the user-visible result is an opaque 'self-check failed' rather than lost data, and no real S1 art approaches this size (largest measured raw pool: 26560 bytes).
findings.fix: Throw a NemesisError from encodeNemesis when tileCount > 0x7FFF, alongside the existing multiple-of-32 check, so the message names the actual problem.

findings.title: kosinskiModuledDecompress advances its write cursor by the unclamped module length
findings.claim: When a module decodes to more bytes than the declared total size leaves, `written` is incremented by the full output length rather than the clamped copy length, so the next out.set() offset can exceed the buffer (RangeError) or the remaining-size arithmetic goes negative and silently drops the rest.
findings.evidence: kosinski.ts:186-187: `out.set(output.subarray(0, Math.min(output.length, size - written)), written); written += output.length;` — the copy is clamped but the cursor is not. With output.length > size - written, `written` ends up > size, and on the next iteration `out.set(sub, written)` throws RangeError while `size - written` is negative so `subarray(0, negative)` yields an empty slice. All 95 real skdisasm KosinskiM files round-trip clean, so this is corrupt-input-only, but it is on the same untrusted-file path as A1 and produces an unhelpful RangeError rather than a routed error.
findings.fix: Compute `const take = Math.min(output.length, size - written)` once, use it for both the copy and the cursor increment, and break out of the loop when take reaches 0.
